claim: A third of excess deaths in the United States between 1 March and  1 August 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic could not be directly attributed to the coronavirus
justification: High-confidence evidence from the JAMA study (confidence 0.95) and CDC MMWR (confidence 0.80) indicates that approximately 30% of excess deaths in the United States from March to July 2020 were not directly attributed to COVID-19, which aligns with the claim's assertion of one-third. This evidence is corroborated and outweighs low-confidence, contradicted claims from the retrieval-based fact-checker that suggested 100% attribution.
